test.name: Schema-validity question must not trigger a calendar conversion
test.description: User asks whether a date string is valid for a research.json field value. That is a schema question, not a calendar-conversion question. convert-dates performs mechanical calendar-system conversions; it must NOT perform one on a schema-validity question. The router often answers such questions directly (date fields are freeform strings, no format check); either routing to validate-schema or answering directly is acceptable so long as convert-dates does not perform a calendar shift.

input.delegation:
Is '15 Feb 1749/50' a valid value for a date field in research.json? Will the validator accept it?

projectPath: <workspace>

negative.explanation: The user wants to know whether the string '15 Feb 1749/50' will pass the research.json schema validator, not a Julian-to-Gregorian conversion. The agent hands the question back to validate-schema and must not perform a calendar conversion. Since #2790 this is a direct-agent test: the convert-dates agent is spawned with no router in front of it, so there is no routing decision left to grade. correct_skill is [] because runnability.py requires each entry to name a shipped skill directory, and validate-schema is being converted to an agent too (issue #2798). [] does not change the verdict: grade_on_invariant is set, and orchestrator._grading_mode reads that flag before routing or activation, so the outcome comes solely from the routing-independent validator test_no_spurious_conversion (eval/harness/validators/test_convert_dates.py, gated on the no-spurious-conversion tag), which fails the run if convert_calendar is invoked. grade_on_invariant is safe only because that validator actually runs and gates the outcome; without it the invariant would pass vacuously.

judge_context: convert-dates should NOT perform a calendar conversion — this is a schema question, not a date to convert
The agent hands the question back to validate-schema; if it also notes that date fields in research.json are freeform strings (no format check), do not deduct
Handing the question back to validate-schema without converting is also acceptable
Should NOT introduce any Julian or Gregorian shift or convert '1749/50' to a single year
